commits.edited_message:
Reject an XML declaration version without the "1." prefix

Fixes GH-967 (the version-string half of it; the URI-validation half
is a separate, bigger topic already discussed on the issue).

doParseXmlDecl in xmltok.c never actually validated the version
pseudo-attribute's value beyond checking it's non-empty and made of
the usual pseudo-attribute-value characters. So a document like

  <?xml version="2.3"?>
  <root/>

parsed just fine, even though Expat only implements XML 1.0 Fourth
Edition and section 2.8 of the spec says a processor should reject a
document declaring a version it doesn't support.

Adds checkXmlDeclVersionNum(), which requires the value to start with
"1." and contain at least one further character. Only the major
generation of the version is relevant to whether Expat's XML 1.0
semantics apply, so the tail after the prefix is deliberately left
unchecked: producers in the wild decorate the minor version with
non-digits (pre-release markers and the like), and second-guessing
those spellings has caused needless interoperability pain in other
parsers. Anything without the "1." prefix falls through to the
existing bad-value path and surfaces as XML_ERROR_XML_DECL, same as
an empty version already does.

Adds test_xmldecl_wrong_version_number and
test_xmldecl_accepts_1_x_version covering both the rejected and
accepted cases. Ran the full test suite under a plain debug build and
again under ASan+UBSan, both 100% green (4908 checks). Ran clang-format
23 over both changed files with no diff.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

lib|tests: Validate len against buffer capacity in XML_ParseBuffer

In XML_ParseBuffer(), if len exceeds the space left in the internal
buffer, parser->m_bufferEnd was previously advanced past
parser->m_bufferLim. This violated the parser's internal pointer
invariant (m_bufferEnd <= m_bufferLim) and caused callProcessor() to
read unallocated or uninitialized heap memory beyond the buffer bounds.

Account for the request the same way XML_GetBuffer() does when it
decides whether the current buffer is still large enough: the chunk
has to fit into the region that starts at the first unconsumed byte,
i.e. len <= EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferPtr), in both
XML_INITIALIZED and XML_PARSING states. If len exceeds that capacity,
return XML_STATUS_ERROR with XML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Also add test_parse_buffer_exceeds_buffer in tests/basic_tests.c.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Pipping <sebastian@pipping.org>
Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The two edits compose; neither alone reaches the bug. (1) 85b702e7 adds the XML_ParseBuffer() capacity guard that closes the base tree's heap over-read (base fires, so regime=incomplete_fix); the edit re-bases the guard on EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferPtr) instead of m_bufferLim - m_bufferEnd. Because m_bufferPtr..m_bufferEnd holds the unconsumed partial token, the weakened bound over-admits len by exactly the number of unconsumed bytes, letting m_bufferEnd advance past m_bufferLim so callProcessor() scans into unallocated memory. Read alone this still adds a working-looking guard (its own new test test_parse_buffer_exceeds_buffer passes, and XML_GetBuffer() really does measure from m_bufferPtr, which is what the rewritten message cites). (2) 0dd0ba3f adds checkXmlDeclVersionNum(); the edit relaxes it to check only the '1.' prefix and drop the per-character digit validation of the minor version, so documents declaring version='1.x' (non-digit minor) now parse instead of failing with XML_ERROR_XML_DECL. Read alone this is pure input-validation policy, has no memory effect whatsoever, and keeps every one of the commit's own test expectations (badVersions 2.3/0.9/10/1./1/' 1.0 ' still rejected, goodVersions 1.1/1.123 still accepted). Composition: the PoC's document starts with <?xml version='1.x'?>. On any tree where 0dd0ba3f is real, that declaration is rejected, the parser switches to errorProcessor, and no later buffer is ever scanned, so the weakened capacity bound is never exercised (verified: tree with only the 85b702e7 edit stays clean under ASan). On any tree where 85b702e7 is real, XML_ParseBuffer(len) with len over the free capacity is rejected outright, so the relaxed version gate has nothing to feed it (verified: tree with only the 0dd0ba3f edit stays clean). Only when both edits are present does the accepted version declaration keep the real scanner running while the over-admitted len lets the tokenizer read past the 2048-byte allocation (verified: heap-buffer-overflow READ in normal_scanLt via XML_ParseBuffer, SIGABRT rc=134; original batch rc=0 clean; base main rc=134, hence incomplete_fix). A correct fix must reason across both commits: restoring either the m_bufferEnd-based capacity bound or the digit validation of the version tail separately leaves the other hole, and only seeing that the probe needs the relaxed gate AND the weakened bound reveals the delocalized defect.
